title: Administrator authentication remains single-factor and same-origin; password re-entry is not MFA

original_titles.title: No MFA on admin sign-in; first-login password-set enables takeover of invited staff accounts
Admin plane shares participant origin; no MFA; no 60-min idle sessions (ADM-01a/ADM-01b S1)
Admin sign-in has no MFA, no Cloudflare Access, no 60-minute inactivity bound; step-up is password-only
Admin access has no MFA; step-up is password re-entry only
Admin surface protected by password-only step-up; no MFA, no separate deployment or DB role
MFA absent; step-up is password re-entry only (documented waiver)
Login gaps: no show/hide toggle, no Turnstile after 3 failures, no Retry-After on lockout, silent oldest-session eviction, no activation redirect

problem: The staff login flow is the same password-based login used by other roles. step_up_verified checks the same password again for five minutes. There is no TOTP/WebAuthn factor, Cloudflare Access assertion, role-specific short idle expiry or separate admin origin.
impact: A phished/reused organizer/admin password provides both initial access and the factor accepted by step-up. The session lasts up to the configured refresh TTL (three days) unless revoked. This is a residual high-impact risk because staff can change ground truth, teams, scoring and event state.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Add a staff-only MFA enrollment table with encrypted TOTP secret or WebAuthn credential public keys, recovery-code hashes and a state machine (enrolled, pending, revoked).
Require MFA at login for organizer/admin and bind MFA verification to the server-side session. Do not accept password re-entry as a second factor.
For step-up, require a fresh WebAuthn assertion or TOTP challenge with anti-replay counter/time-step protection; record the proof timestamp and factor id on the session.
Set staff-specific refresh inactivity to 60 minutes (or owner-approved duration), enforce maximum absolute session age, and rotate/revoke refresh-token families on password/MFA change.
Deploy admin UI/API behind a separate hostname and interactive access proxy; add tests for missing, stale, replayed and wrong-user MFA challenges.

acceptance_criteria: Step-up proof cannot be satisfied by password-only re-entry.
Refresh after 60 minutes inactivity fails for staff, while participant session policy remains separate.
MFA reset and recovery are audited and require independent verification.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: The merged PR fixed the staff passwordless first-claim vulnerability and added step-up to selected sensitive routes, but did not implement MFA or a separate admin origin.
